office_does: A State Representative writes and votes on Washington state law and the operating, capital and transportation budgets, covering school funding, tax structure, housing rules, health funding and criminal-justice statutes.
race_blurb: Open seat left by retiring Rep. Jenny Graham. Former Spokane City Councilmember Jonathan Bingle, endorsed by Graham, won a majority in the primary and faces first-time Democratic candidate Julia Payne; they split on income taxes, spending, gender policy and data centers.

candidates.summary: Republican former Spokane City Councilmember (2022-2025), small-business owner and pastor, running on lower taxes, public safety, treatment-first homelessness policy and parental rights.
highlights: Opposes all forms of income tax and proposes zero-based budgeting and performance audits [S9]
On the council, helped criminalize open drug use and make being in parks after hours arrestable [S2]
Proposed council restrictions on transgender bathroom access, sports and gender-affirming care for minors [S2]
Platform calls for parental notification in all school matters and full curriculum transparency [S9]

taxes.basis: Pledges to oppose all income taxes including capital gains and new 'fees', and to reduce the tax burden.

spending.basis: Zero-based budgeting and audits; would cut anything not tied to infrastructure or physical safety; calls homelessness spending a failure.

housing.basis: Blames regulation and impact fees for costs and backs market-led supply; council votes to drop parking mandates and downtown height limits.

safety.basis: Council record criminalizing open drug use and park-hours violations; platform of tougher penalties and treatment-first homelessness policy.

climate.basis: Would repeal or roll back the Climate Commitment Act and opposes carbon policies that raise fuel costs.

local-control.basis: Would stop unfunded state mandates on cities and counties and top-down mandates that bypass local representatives.

social.basis: Council amendment and platform to ban gender-affirming treatment for minors and restrict trans participation in girls' sports; supports a 13-week abortion limit.

parental-rights.basis: Platform calls for full curriculum transparency, parental notification in all school matters and school choice.

experience.basis: One Spokane City Council term (2022-2025); no legislative tenure; opponent is a first-time candidate.

candidates.summary: First-time Democratic candidate, office administrator and long-time Spokane Pride volunteer, running on affordability, accessibility and constituent access.
highlights: Supports the Millionaire's Tax and a more graduated tax code [S6][S5]
Supports banning data-center construction unless strict self-sufficiency requirements are met [S6]
Favors a universal health care approach to address provider shortages [S5]

taxes.basis: Supports the Millionaire's Tax, 'more creative revenue options' and graduated taxation of those with means.

spending.basis: Would direct new progressive revenue to programs such as child care and fully fund firefighting.

safety.basis: Calls for higher accountability standards for police and a mix of treatment-first and housing-first approaches; calls protester prosecutions unjust.

healthcare.basis: Says a universal health care approach would help fix the mental-health provider shortage.

tech.basis: Supports a ban on data-center construction unless strict sustainability requirements are met, plus comprehensive regulation.

social.basis: Spokane Pride volunteer and board officer, endorsed by Stonewall Democrats and Planned Parenthood Advocates; no policy statement of her own.

experience.basis: First-time candidate with no prior office, running on lived experience.
